entries.name: Jennie
entries.lead: Machine knitting is addictive. Don't say I didn't warn you!
items: Don't feel guilty about your massive yarn stash. We've all got one!
You are not alone! We've ALL struggled, we've ALL made mistakes, so don't feel you are stupid or silly if something goes wrong.

Modern knitting machines can do so much it is tempting to plunge in and try and conquer everything TO-DAY. Slow down, take time to get really familiar with the basics, practice new techniques and master just one machine first.
Machine knitting is addictive. Don't say I didn't warn you!
Make the most of Knit It Now - it's the most fantastic resource with lots of help, ideas and fun for every machine knitter.

entries.name: Jacqueline
entries.lead: It is a 'high maintenance hobby' this is not something you can really do once in a while
items: Machine knitting is not like knitting in a rocking chair. It is more like you as a pilot with your aircraft or you as a SCUBA diver with your air supply. You are having an experience with a machine, not a tool. This has sophisticated mechanics that need to be understood to be used well.
Have your pre-flight checklist : all clean, lubricated, straight needles, resilient sponge bar, yarn that plays nicely with the feeders, carriages and needles, weights that make sense

In-flight activities should be made pleasurable. Will you love managing the machine and yarn. Will you enjoy finding the right pace. Are you happy to keep your eyes pealed for problems and fix them early before small problems become big problems.

Post flight : How well you end one machine knitting session will determine how nice it is to start the next. Make it clear via notes, and placement of all the pieces to pick up seamlessly where you left off

It is a 'high maintenance 'hobby' this is not something you can really do once in a while and then when you have 20 min. It has a consuming effect on your space and time. If there are 10 other hobbies in your life this will probably not fly.

entries.name: Elaine
entries.lead: Ravel Cord, Label Your Tools, Ribbing Tip
items: Where to get Ravel Cord: In the US, Hobby Lobby has a large collection of slippery cord. For std gauge machines, I use dental floss that is nicely waxed!

Label your tools: If it's a 1/3 prong tool, label the 1 end with "3" and the 3 end with "1", and so on with all the tools, so when they are in the tool holder, you know what's hidden, as all three tools are different -- a 1/2, a 2/3 and a 3/1. If you have two two prongs sticking up, you don't have to guess which has the 1 prong and which has the 2 prong.

How to make ribbing with waste yarn, then use 1 circle with ravel cord. After that, make your zigzag row, two or three circular rows, and knit the rib. There is much less flair on the bottom. Ribbing Cast on Methods
